description: The G2P network's words from the books listeners hear (picovox_train/g2p.py load_data, every stage; python -m picovox_train.g2p book counts a book): labels - pronunciations of the books' words the dictionary lacks or has wrong (a dictionary word's label replaced, its rule-labeled forms following): names as well-established English pronunciations (anglicized Spanish as American readers say it, CMUdict's own convention - QUIXOTE K IY0 HH OW1 T IY0, SENOR S IY2 N Y AO1 R) and the archaic and British words' standard pronunciations, each a dictionary word in training; books - each book's word counts (the front end's words that train: the dictionary's, the labels', and their possessives - a possessive the dictionary lacks takes its stem's target with its -s suffix), frequency weights with g2p-words.json weightCounts. Wikipedia's words outside the dictionary are labeled by Wiktionary where it has them (7,499 words - its first American pronunciation, else its first untagged one, that has an R for each of the spelling's r's: the kaikki.org extract of 2026-10-30; written in the dictionary's conventions - its reduced vowels and secondary stress - by a network trained on the words both have, where that changes nothing else), and the most frequent of the rest by hand (903 of the 1,000 most frequent words of Wikipedia's that had no label and aren't a known word's regular form - names and terms, as the books' names are labeled: QURAN K ER0 AA1 N, MUGHAL M UW1 G AH0 L; the network read 58% of them another way; and eight of its most frequent words in capitals that are read as words, or that a rule had labeled wrong - FIFA, LIGO, UEFA; HTTPS, its letters, not HTTP's plural); heldOut - a tenth of Wiktionary's words held out of the labels, those that aren't the words file's (507 words that never train): a measure of the words the network hasn't seen (g2p.py evaluate - the held-out WER).
